text:
Leah: Quick sync — after yesterday's canary we saw oscillating evictions on node-3: pages evicted, then refetched within 20-50ms, repeating and causing extra PCIe churn. want to discuss a residency scoring + lease extension approach to dampen churn.
Omar: yeah saw that. root cause seems to be eviction decisions made purely on instantaneous hot-score; no short-term memory. when hotness bounces (bursty traffic) we thrash.
Nina: idea: add a short "recent-access" credit to residency score that decays over time. score = base_hot + alpha*recent_credit - beta*resident_cost. recent_credit gets a boost on access and decays with half-life 150ms.
Vik: that helps, but need to ensure memory pressure still respected. propose combining that with a soft-lease: when we evict, mark object with a lease_ts = now + lease_ms. if a request accesses it before lease_ts expires, instead of immediate refill we consult policy: allow one cheap recompute or defer refill to avoid immediate re-pinning.
Leah: can we generalize: residency_score = access_freq_weight * freq + recency_weight * recency_score - eviction_cost_weight * cost + lease_bonus? then eviction prefers low score.
Omar: yes. also add tenant_priority multiplier to prevent low-priority tenants holding onto leases. tenant_priority in [0.5,2.0].
Nina: implementation note: store recency_score and lease_ts inside page metadata; keep updates lock-free-ish using seq counters. avoid touching big maps on every access.
Vik: policy knobs: lease_ms default 200, lease_backoff_ms for repeated refaults, score_half_life_ms 150, eviction_cost_weight default 1.2. Need sensible defaults.
Leah: what about fairness — if a premium tenant creates bursty access and uses leases frequently, do we starve others? we already have tenant quotas but leases complicate it.
Omar: track cumulative_lease_bytes per-tenant windowed (1m). if tenant exceeds lease_budget, reduce their tenant_priority multiplier gradually. recharge over time.
Nina: metrics to add: lease_refault_rate, lease_saved_evictions, lease_bytes_granted, tenant_lease_debt, residency_score_histogram. Also monitor refetch_latency when leases prevent eager refill.
Vik: failure modes: inaccurate eviction_cost (we underestimate recompute cost) => bad UX. fallback: if estimator unavailable, use conservative default (high cost) to avoid evicting expensive items. log estimator confidence.
Leah: ops: plan a canary behind feature flag on 3 nodes with lease_ms=200, score_half_life_ms=150. rollback if p99 tail increases by >1.5x.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: canary-cluster-3 nodes [3,4,5] at 02:30 UTC. Auto-rollback on p99 > 1.5x baseline for 5m.
Omar: dev tasks: (1) residency metadata fields + lock-free updates, (2) scoring function & config, (3) tenant lease accounting, (4) metrics + dashboards. I'll take (1),(3).
Nina: I'll prototype scoring function and add estimator hooks. Vik: you own canary and dashboards. Leah: I'll write short RFC with equations, config, and safety gates.
Leah: timeline: RFC today, patch next week, canary after tests. Thanks all — ping in thread when RFC is up. :thumbsup:
